title: Which Country Has The Best Schools?

blanks.sentence: The OECD carries out the Pisa tests _____.
The tests compare teaching in maths, science and _____.
At first, comparing countries through Pisa caused _____.
Some critics questioned the _____ of comparing very different countries.
A common pattern is that top-performing countries tend to be _____.
Large Western European countries are being _____ by faster-rising places.
Pisa is defended as a way to measure readiness for a _____.
Successful systems help all pupils reach a _____.
This should happen regardless of students’ _____.
Estonia avoids teaching students by separate levels because it does not want to _____ them.

multipleChoice.question: What do the Pisa tests try to measure?
options: How much schools spend on education
How effectively countries teach key school subjects
How satisfied students are with teachers
How many students enter university

multipleChoice.question: Why were the Pisa rankings controversial when introduced?
options: They were only available in small countries
They ignored maths and science completely
They were designed by individual schools
People doubted whether very different places could be compared

multipleChoice.question: What pattern is mentioned in the rankings?
options: Smaller countries often appear among the strongest performers
Western Europe always leads the tables
Large countries are excluded from the rankings
Only English-speaking countries perform well

multipleChoice.question: How are places such as Singapore, Estonia and Taiwan described in relation to larger European countries?
options: Too small to be considered rivals
Historically dominant economic powers
Fast-rising competitors that outperform them
Countries with weaker school systems

multipleChoice.question: What is meant by a knowledge economy here?
options: An economy based mainly on farming
An economy relying on highly educated workers in skilled industries
A system where students study only technology
A ranking that measures national income

multipleChoice.question: What factor is introduced as helping countries do well in Pisa?
options: Allowing only top students to take tests
Dividing all pupils by ability from the start
Focusing mostly on private schools
Prioritising getting every pupil to a certain level

multipleChoice.question: What does Sean say successful systems do?
options: They ensure pupils reach a standard whatever their background
They select pupils according to family background
They remove reading from the curriculum
They measure only the strongest students

multipleChoice.question: What is Rando Kuustik’s view of teaching students by different ability levels?
options: It is the only way to improve scores
It is useful if done internationally
It separates people in a way schools should avoid
It has no connection with Estonia’s success

multipleChoice.question: In the phrase “regardless of their background”, what is being treated as not a barrier?
options: The country’s population size
Pupils’ personal or social background
The school’s test schedule
The language used in the exam

multipleChoice.question: What broader idea does Estonia’s example support?
options: Elite separation is essential for top rankings
School success depends only on national wealth
Large countries should not take Pisa tests
Inclusive education can be linked to strong performance
